label: Kitchen / Hearth Room
volunteer_identification_guide: Cooking space identified by large chimney breast, hearth, colonial oven, flue hole, water supply, or meathooks.

label: Parlor / Sitting Room
volunteer_identification_guide: Formal living room facing primary facade; finer joinery, moulded timber skirting, ornamental mantelpiece, decorative plaster ceiling rose.

label: Bedroom
volunteer_identification_guide: Private sleeping quarters; smaller dimensions, wardrobe recesses, fireplace in master bedroom, plainer skirtings.

label: Pantry / Larder / Store
volunteer_identification_guide: Cool food storage room often on south or shaded side; fitted with timber shelving, meat safes, and mesh ventilation.

label: Central Hallway / Passage
volunteer_identification_guide: Circulation corridor dividing formal front rooms; fanlight above front door, timber wainscot or plaster archway.

label: Enclosed Verandah Room / Sleepout
volunteer_identification_guide: Space created by enclosing former open verandah with louvres, weatherboards, or fibro; sloped ceiling following verandah pitch, step in floor level.

label: Shearing Board (Woolshed)
volunteer_identification_guide: Working line where sheep are shorn; slatted or hardwood plank floor, friction drive wheels, bracket mounts on rafters, counting-out chutes.

label: Wool Classing / Baling Room
volunteer_identification_guide: Expansive clear-span room with large classing table, wool bins, screw/lever/hydraulic wool press, scale markings, and load-out doorway.

label: Sweat Pen (Holding Area)
volunteer_identification_guide: Internal slatted timber grates (battens) allowing waste to drop into underfloor pit while keeping fleece clean before shearing.

label: Tack & Harness Room
volunteer_identification_guide: Service room in stables fitted with wooden peg racks for bridles, saddle trees, collar pegs, and grease pots.

label: Compacted Earth / Packed Clay
volunteer_identification_guide: Beaten dirt or clay floor mixed with ox blood, fat, or salt for binding; common in pioneer huts, blacksmiths, and early sheds.

label: Stone Flags / Sandstone Paving
volunteer_identification_guide: Large flat sandstone or slate flags laid directly on sand bed; cold, durable floor for kitchens, pantries, and dairies.

label: Brick Paving (Sand Bed)
volunteer_identification_guide: Handmade or pressed bricks laid flat or on edge on sand; typical of detached kitchens, cellars, and stables.

label: Timber Slats / Grates (Woolshed)
volunteer_identification_guide: Narrow hardwood battens spaced 15-20mm apart to allow dung and urine to fall through to ground void underneath.

label: Butt-jointed Timber Boards (No T&G)
volunteer_identification_guide: Rectangular hardwood boards planed on 3 sides only; boards abut squarely without interlocking tongue; thin steel ruler slides straight through gap into sub-floor void.

label: Tongue & Groove (T&G) Milled Boards
volunteer_identification_guide: Milled boards with tongue on one edge and groove on opposite; steel ruler stops ~5mm into gap; 150mm wide c. 1865-1890s; 146mm/100mm c. 1890-1920s.

label: Concrete Slab Floor
volunteer_identification_guide: Mass or steel-reinforced concrete pad; modern replacement or industrial floor in dairies and workshops.

label: Linoleum / Floorcloth Remnant
volunteer_identification_guide: Linseed-oil based floorcloth (post-1864) tacked to boards with brass tacks; pattern layers preserved in cupboard bases.

label: Unlined (Exposed Framing / Masonry)
volunteer_identification_guide: Internal frame studs, split slabs, pise, or brickwork left completely exposed without cosmetic covering.

label: Horizontal Timber Lining Boards
volunteer_identification_guide: Wide rough-sawn or dressed boards nailed horizontally to internal studs; may be beaded or plain splayed.

label: Vertical V-Joint (VJ) Boards
volunteer_identification_guide: Milled tongue-and-groove boards with bevelled edge forming V-shaped shadow groove; standard late Victorian/Federation interior lining.

label: Hessian / Calico Sacking & Wallpaper
volunteer_identification_guide: Hessian or flour sacking tacked across timber studs with blued tacks, pasted with newspaper and patterned wallpaper layers.

label: Lath & Plaster
volunteer_identification_guide: Horizontal split or sawn timber laths nailed to studs, coated with 2-3 coats of lime/sand plaster mixed with animal horsehair.

label: Pressed Metal (Wunderlich)
volunteer_identification_guide: Decorative stamped zinc/steel panels manufactured by Wunderlich or Rocke; ornate floral, diaper, or classical patterns.

label: Ripple Iron Lining
volunteer_identification_guide: Miniature corrugated iron panels fixed horizontally or vertically as durable rodent-proof lining in kitchens and meathouses.

label: Fibro / Masonite / Cane-ite / Gyprock
volunteer_identification_guide: Manufactured sheet wallboards: Masonite (compressed hardboard, post-1930), Cane-ite (soft sugarcane board, post-1939), Gyprock plasterboard (post-1940).

label: Limewash on Masonry / Earth
volunteer_identification_guide: Sanitary slaked lime coating applied directly to internal brick, pise, or stone walls; repeated coats create rounded corners.

label: Open Brick / Stone Fireplace Hearth
volunteer_identification_guide: Wide masonry opening with iron chimney crane or pot hook bar for suspension of iron kettles and camp ovens.

label: Colonial Oven (Open Grate + Side Oven)
volunteer_identification_guide: Cast-iron or sheet-iron oven box built directly into side of open fireplace, heated by flue gases from open fire.

label: Cast-iron Range / Kitchener
volunteer_identification_guide: Freestanding or recessed cast-iron cooking range (Metters Dover, Bega, Galliers & Klaerr, Albion) with enclosed firebox, hob plates, and oven.

label: Kerosene / Acetylene Gas Fittings
volunteer_identification_guide: Hanging brass ceiling pullies for kerosene lamps or copper piping from external calcium carbide acetylene generator.

label: Early Surface Electric (Twisted Pair / Cleats)
volunteer_identification_guide: Twisted cotton-braided electrical wiring mounted on ceramic barrel insulators and timber mounting blocks; brass tumbler switches.

label: Lead / Galvanised Iron Water Pipe & Sink
volunteer_identification_guide: Early gravity water reticulation with soldered lead or threaded galvanised iron piping and brass bibcock taps over enamel/iron sink.
